chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: How recording dates and society gigs were staffed
summary: Leaders like Red Allen or Teddy Wilson picked particular players for each date, so personnels changed from session to session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now

blocks.x: together (inaudible) talking about there. And we did some other gigs. We used to do hotel gigs together, like with different band leaders, you know. Guys like Snowden. Whoever got the gig together -- you know, whoever would come in. The call would come in and they had a gig, we would work for these guys. Now, recording back in those days, just like what you're talking about now -- only recording we did was (inaudible) what - like Teddy Wilson. Different guys would get these recording dates and maybe use all the top men. Like they get the top groups and put a group combo together, and they'd go and back up some singer, or they'd get a gig. It wasn't a lot of recording going around. Just only top jazz men, and, like, you know -- Red Allen would get a gig, or Teddy Wilson was recording a lot, you know. These fellows here, if they got a recording date, you could probably get on a recording date.

Remember a lot of recording dates -- a lot of Red Allen dates had different musicians. These are musicians they put together for these different dates.
Why they would do this was because they would have something they would want to do -- certain things that they would want to do, they'd want to use this particular musician.
Because they just use him, they may want to get a different sound. They want to use, like, a different set-up of musicians to give them what they want.
And I noticed that Teddy Wilson did that a lot, you know. He would use, like different musicians behind different singers like, you know.
And it was good. And that's the way we did, you know, back in the 30's and things like that.
They would have a gig for a hotel. They would use certain musicians for this hotel, because they want to play this certain type of music.
And they would want maybe a smooth type

of a band, you know. (inaudible) where they would use a jazz group, they would put together like a society band. It would be some of these jazz musicians, but these were the type of musicians that they would want to use. "Hey, we're playing for Miss Vanderbilt so and so." So they would pick the musicians that they want to use for this gig. If you had a recording date coming up, you would pick the men that you want. You would tell me, "Look, can you get me the drummer so and so, I'd like to use him?" "I'd like to use so and so on tenor. I'd like to use so and so on trumpet," you know. "I'd like to use so and so on banjo or guitar." This where they would put this band together for this particular thing. That's why you see in your book you have different musicians on a lot of different dates, you know. Always changing for the ideas that they want. (inaudible)
